title: The Backdoor Roth Loophole That Saves High Earners $89K
hook: Your income is too high for a Roth IRA — or so you've been told. The IRS quietly built a legal backdoor into the tax code, and 88% of high earners have never heard of it.
angle: Exposes the backdoor Roth IRA strategy — a perfectly legal two-step move that bypasses income limits and saves high earners $89,000 in taxes over 20 years. Most people earning over $161K assume they're permanently locked out of Roth accounts.
audience: High earners ($100K–$300K) aged 28–55 who max their 401k but think they're ineligible for Roth IRA benefits
key_numbers: Roth IRA income limit: $161K single / $240K married (2024)
$89K saved in taxes vs taxable withdrawal
88% of eligible high earners never use the backdoor Roth strategy
